answer: A sybil swarm stalls when agents must join the beacon-anchored kernel work registry before trading. First, it publishes one kernel fingerprint tied to a hardware key and stakes 60 tokens. Second, a beacon sets a fresh proof puzzle daily, verified by two established peers within six hours. Third, its limit grows only after twenty-one clean days, while cheating burns the stake and blocks the fingerprint for 120 days. One fake costs about $910; 1,000 fakes need $910,000 and 9,000 hours of verified work. Like a plume betraying a hidden fire, a forged entry draws attention instead of hiding.
